31.80% is the 2001-11 decadal growth of urban population (286 to 377.1 million), while 31.16% is the urban share of India's population in Census 2011; confusing the two is a common trap.

Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai are diversified towns. Shimla, Ooty and Araku are resort towns; Raniganj, Digboi and Khammam are mining/collection towns; Tirupati, Varanasi and Rameswaram are religious/cultural towns.
Residual Andhra Pradesh was 29.47% urban in 2011, making it the least urbanised southern State. 47.45% is the urban share of Visakhapatnam, the most urbanised district.

Pairs 1-3 are correct: Koyas live in the Godavari basin agency, Konda Reddis in the Godavari hill tracts (Rampa), and Konda Doras in the Visakhapatnam agency. Pair 4 is wrong: the Nallamala forest is the Chenchu habitat; Yanadis live on the southern coastal plains around Pulicat Lake (Nellore, Chittoor).
